citations.assessment: Rav Amemar bar Mar Yenuka reports having stood before Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Avya. The Bavli names his father. The longer genealogy is the local edition’s compilation.
The reciprocal article names Mar Yenuka and Mar Keshisha as sons of Rav Chisda. The Almanac records a conflicting father of Mar Yenuka and questions it.

The Almanac does report the killing by the Persian king and, in the same paragraph, questions the genealogical wording it quotes. It reports differently numbered years from Tzemach David and Sherira; Sherira separately reports the execution in Adar following arrest in Tevet. Leave the dates as witnessed.
Amemar proposes restoring daily recitation of the Decalogue. Rav Ashi refers to the objection involving sectarians.
Amemar institutes a skipping pattern for recitation of the festival offerings in Nehardea. This is separate from the Decalogue.
Rav Ashi objects when a woman summoned in Nehardea does not follow Amemar to Mechoza and he issues a writ against her.
Amemar is a Nehardean, but extends return of an assessment beyond their twelve-month limit.
Amemar describes himself as a Nehardean and permits a revised plea.
The checked Bavli reads Rav Acha bar Rav addressing Ravina. The local English must keep bar Rava as the edition’s explicit conjecture.

Ravnai reports Shmuel that witness and judge can combine. Amemar praises the teaching and Rav Ashi asserts Rava already refuted it. The text of the Bavli says your mother’s father. The name Rami bar Chama is Heilprin’s parenthesis.
The reciprocal notice accords with the editorial identification of Amemar’s maternal grandfather. The distinct sources for names and for kinship are kept local.
All three are at Azgur’s gate. Rav Ashi is the one who sees Mar Zutra affected by the smell. Zevachim 19a depicts a separate Persian court encounter.
The Mar Zutra entry gives a longer version of the same episode. It cites Ketubot 61b whereas the incident starts at 61a in the checked foliation.

The Bavli has Ashi ask what happens if the father dies and the profit-bearing document falls to the heirs. This is the origin of the separate narrative. The piety and speaker glosses are the local parentheses.
Amemar permits Huna’s marriage and Rav Ashi challenges the lineage presumption. The passage itself names Rav Zevid of Nehardea as Amemar’s source.
Rav Ashi sits before Amemar, explicitly addressing him as mar.
Rav Ashi asks about eye treatment; the Sabbath discussion supplies the title mar.
Amemar transmits Rav Zevid’s ruling about three tendons.
Tosafot give the chronology and already propose indirect transmission. The next source-edition clause challenges it with the Rav Acha report.
The objection relies on using the local adjusted patronym; the digital Bavli gives bar Rav.
The checked Bavli already encloses Amemar said in parentheses. It reports Pumbedita’s elders ruling like Shmuel.
Maharshal’s corrected text runs straight from the feast to the elders. The attributed deletion is therefore supported in the checked digital gloss.
The checked Bavli names Rav Sheshet. The Rif names Rav Ashi in the parallel; leave both attributions distinct and preserve Heilprin’s chronological difficulty.
The Bavli gives the first-person Nehardean formula but not elder here. The court scene separately shows Amemar exercising judicial authority. The complete Yuchasin source still awaits collation.
Direct reciprocal Seder HaDorot pointer; it does not independently verify the Yuchasin passage.

In both variants Gamda addresses the seated group of Amemar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi. The reciprocal Heilprin entry 866 names Rav Zevid in its lead-in, while the Bavli names him separately.
Amemar expressly cites Rav Dimi of Nehardea regarding the inspection of an animal after a fall.
The repeated transmission is consistent with the already cited tendon ruling.
Amemar relates saying the teaching before Rav Zevid of Nehardea; Kiddushin also names him. Leave Zevid with and without the place name as separate source forms.
Amemar cites Rav Chama on paying a widow and a creditor when both land and cash are available.
Rav Yeimar appears before Amemar to testify for Mar Zutra.
The checked source reads Amemar; the edition explicitly spells Marimar here. Preserve the local form.
Amemar transmits Rav Pappa’s rule about placing fatty tissue on meat.
Ravina quotes Amemar, whose report names Marimar in the name of Rav Dimi. Preserve both source name forms and the full direction in the supporting comparison.
Amemar transmits Rava’s lung blister comparison ruling.
